clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside northern Chile

clues.text: The Atacama Desert wraps all around this town. It gets almost no rain in a whole year.
clues.narrowing: rules out wet places and points to the dry desert north

clues.text: This town is a department capital in Honduras. It serves as the chief town of its department.

source.quote: is the capital city and a municipality of the same name of the department of Intibucá, Honduras.

clues.text: This town is famed for the coolest climate in Honduras. Its air stays cooler than anywhere else there.
clues.narrowing: rules out warmer towns in Honduras

source.quote: La Esperanza is famous for having the coolest climate in Honduras.

clues.text: This town is the newer of two twin towns. The older twin began as a Lenca town.
clues.narrowing: rules out towns that did not grow beside an older twin

source.quote: Intibucá is the older of the twin cities and was originally an indigenous Lenca community, while La Esperanza is the newer ladino community.

clues.text: Lenca hands still shape fine clay pots here. A marked trail links towns that keep this craft alive.
clues.narrowing: rules out places off the Lenca craft trail

source.quote: Sites on the Lenca Trail have been designated by the government and United Nations development in order to encourage more cultural tourism, and help create new markets for the traditional crafts, such as pottery, practiced by the Lenca, in order to preserve their culture.

clues.text: Two towns here have grown into one city. You cannot tell where one ends and the next begins.
clues.narrowing: confirms the twin towns that grew into one

source.quote: The city of La Esperanza is merged indistinguishably with the city of Intibucá, the head of the neighboring municipality of Intibucá.
